clips.text_zh: 22歲炒狗幣贏錢，230K美金買咗condo，之後食晒，依家返學做工揹返晒啲債。兄弟…你呢？condo都係另一種學費。🙏
clips.text_en_b1: In 2021, when I was 22, I made a bunch of random crypto money from dogecoin. I lived for two years with no job, on a perma vacation, dropped out of school and bought a condo for $230K. Eventually the money ran out. I went back to school, graduated, and now I make $100K and live in my condo.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ anon bought a condo with crypto gains, now stuck with debt

signal.rationale: Life-story post, no actionable trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Back in 2021, when I was 22, I made a decent pile from dogecoin and blew it on two years of perma-vacation. I dropped out, splashed $230K on a condo, and partied until the funds dried up completely. Eventually I went back to school, graduated, and now I earn roughly $100K living in the very unit that drained my crypto gains.
clips.text_en_c1: At twenty-two, having made a considerable sum from speculative dogecoin trades in 2021, I effectively abandoned my studies and embarked on what can only be described as an extended, unearned sabbatical. Within months I had committed $230,000 to a condo purchase, rationalising the outlay as an investment rather than an indulgence. The capital, however, proved far more finite than I had anticipated; by the time I re-enrolled, graduated and entered the workforce, the cycle had reversed. Now twenty-seven, I earn roughly $100K and remain tethered to a mortgage whose monthly burden eclipses any genuine financial freedom.
clips.text_en_c2: At twenty-two, flush from an ill-timed windfall in dogecoin, I liquidated a substantial position and purchased a condominium for $230,000, effectively retiring before I had ever begun. For two gloriously unstructured years I drifted, eschewing employment and academia alike, until the liquidity, as it invariably does, evaporated. I subsequently reenrolled, completed my degree, and now, at twenty-seven, draw a comfortable six-figure salary while still occupying the same ill-advised asset. The condo, now a millstone dressed as a milestone, anchors me to a Sisyphean cycle of labour, consumption, and quiet despair. So here I sit, twenty-seven and ostensibly settled, contemplating whether homeownership at twenty-two was simply an elaborate tuition fee payable to the school of hard knocks, and whether anyone else in this thread finds themselves similarly marooned, gazing at plasterboard ceilings and wondering where the…

clips.text_zh: Musk成日出post搞到成個market震，4chan永遠有人跟。Tesla earnings、FSD、Starship test、Optimus，全部都係我portfolio嘅外圍變數⋯⋯又係命。
clips.text_en_b1: Tesla, SpaceX, Optimus and Musk tweets all move the market every week. /biz/ threads track every Starship test and FSD update. Tesla earnings and delivery numbers always create the next setup. Elon Musk posts something, and the chart reacts in seconds. Right now the focus is on Q3 deliveries and FSD v13 progress.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ general market banter, crypto price targets

signal.rationale: Implicit TSLA interest around earnings/FSD catalysts, no entry level named

clips.text_en_b2: Elon Musk's posts, together with Tesla, SpaceX, and Optimus milestones, routinely send shockwaves through the market, and /biz/ threads track every single development obsessively. Each Starship test or FSD update creates fresh setups that traders scramble to exploit, while Tesla's quarterly earnings and delivery figures almost always trigger the next major move. Right now the focus has shifted toward Q3 delivery numbers and FSD v13 progress, with Musk's X activity still dictating short-term sentiment. His chart reactions are essentially the market's heartbeat.
clips.text_en_c1: Tesla, SpaceX, Optimus and Musk's ceaseless social media activity constitute, for /biz/ regulars at least, an unofficial index that disproportionately influences intraday sentiment across multiple sectors. Dedicated threads track each Starship test, FSD iteration and delivery projection with a fervour that borders on devotional. Quarterly earnings releases and updated guidance invariably generate the next high-conviction setup, while a single post from the man himself can trigger double-digit intraday swings within seconds. At present, attention is squarely on Q3 delivery figures and the incremental rollout of FSD v13, both of which are treated as binary catalysts.
clips.text_en_c2: Elon Musk's social media output has, by degrees, become a de facto macroeconomic signal that retail traders parse with Talmudic devotion. Each perfunctory post precipitates immediate volatility across Tesla's equity, while /biz/ threads dutifully chronicle every incremental Starship static fire and FSD iteration as though they were dispatches from a distant theatre. Quarterly delivery figures and the long-awaited rollout of FSD v13 constitute the present axis around which speculative positioning orbits, with each earnings release functioning as a Schelling point for bulls and bears alike. Optimus updates, once dismissed as vapour, now attract genuine institutional scrutiny. The phenomenon speaks to a broader pathology: in markets this saturated with derivative signals, even the chairman's breakfast musings acquire the gravitas of policy pronouncements, and we, the faithful, parse his every syllable for alpha.

clips.text_zh: Anthropic個researcher走人，話唔想再參與訓練會自我改良嘅AI。wtf。藍領先死、白領後死⋯⋯我考牌做工程師有冇用？🧐
clips.text_en_b1: Jacob Coxon, an Anthropic researcher, said Tuesday he is leaving the company. He does not want to join the industrywide rush to build AI systems that can improve themselves. He is worried such systems could spiral out of control and destroy humanity. He trained new models by feeding them vast amounts of data.
clips.source_hint: /g/ Anthropic researcher quits over AI self-improvement fears

signal.rationale: Tech news, not a trade setup

clips.text_en_b2: Jacob Coxon, a researcher at Anthropic, announced on Tuesday that he is walking away from the company because he refuses to take part in the frantic race to build AI systems capable of improving themselves. He has voiced serious concerns that such models could spiral beyond human control and potentially spell disaster for civilisation. Before departing, he spent his tenure training fresh models by feeding them enormous datasets.
clips.text_en_c1: Jacob Coxon, a researcher whose remit at Anthropic placed him at the coalface of frontier model development, confirmed on Tuesday that he is stepping down from his role. His stated reason is disquiet at the broader industry trajectory—specifically, the accelerating push toward AI systems capable of recursive self-improvement, architectures whose emergent behaviours he considers inadequately constrained. Having personally supervised training pipelines that ingest vast corpora of human-generated data, he evidently concluded that the existential tail risk outweighed the professional upside.
clips.text_en_c2: Jacob Coxon, a researcher of considerable repute at Anthropic, announced his departure this Tuesday, citing an unwillingness to participate in what he characterises as the industry's precipitate race toward self-modifying artificial intelligence. His concerns, articulated with measured sobriety, centre on the possibility that recursive self-improvement could yield systems whose trajectory we can neither anticipate nor arrest, with civilisation itself as the collateral damage. Having personally orchestrated the training of nascent models upon vast corpora of curated data, he brings to his dissent a credibility that dilettante doomsayers conspicuously do not possess. The implications reverberate beyond the laboratory: if credentialed insiders are voting with their feet, what counsel remains for the aspiring engineer contemplating vocational licensure, given that the displaced first will be the blue-collar, followed inexorably by the credentialed white-collar? Existential risk has seldom arrived…

clips.text_zh: 中國話已經做到2nm，仲要唔用EUV機。condo佬同我一樣，根本唔可能贏。lol。Tsinghua同SMIC⋯⋯半導體板塊要小心。
clips.text_en_b1: China has reportedly reached 2nm chip production without using EUV machines. The thread claims it is impossible to compete with Chinese semiconductor progress right now. Anons are debating what this means for ASML, TSMC and Intel, and whether the West has already lost the chip race.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread on China's 2nm breakthrough without EUV
clips.text_en_b2: Reports emerging from China suggest the country has hit 2nm chip production without relying on EUV machines at all, which has sent shockwaves through global semiconductor forums. Anons on /pol/ are hammering out a fierce debate, with many claiming it is now genuinely impossible to keep pace with Chinese progress. The implications for ASML, TSMC, and Intel look severe, since the West's grip on advanced lithography may already be slipping away. Several posters have even suggested shorting semiconductor stocks as a defensive move.
clips.text_en_c1: Reports emerging from Chinese state-affiliated sources suggest that domestic foundries, working in concert with Tsinghua University and SMIC, have achieved functional 2nm silicon production without recourse to ASML's extreme ultraviolet lithography platforms—an achievement that, if independently verified, would constitute a genuine paradigm shift rather than the customary press-release theatre. Anons in the thread are split between those convinced the West has already conceded the semiconductor race and sceptics pointing out that yields, throughput and consistent reproducibility remain undisclosed. The implications for ASML, TSMC and Intel, whose valuations are predicated on assumed technological moats, are, at minimum, uncomfortable to contemplate.
clips.text_en_c2: Reports emanating from ostensibly credible sources suggest that Chinese foundries, principally those affiliated with Tsinghua and SMIC, have achieved commercial-grade 2-nanometre production without recourse to ASML's vaunted EUV lithography, an architectural circumvention that, if substantiated, would constitute a paradigm shift of singular magnitude. The technological implications are staggering; the geopolitical ramifications, frankly, incalculable, given that decades of Western export controls premised upon lithographic supremacy have evidently failed to constrain Beijing's ascent. Anons, ever the nimble tacticians, are now dissecting the ramifications for ASML, TSMC, and Intel with the sanguinity of pallbearers. Whether the chip race has already concluded, or whether the West retains latent capacity for resurgence, remains a matter of spirited contestation, though the prevailing sentiment suggests that semiconductor portfolios require immediate, defensive rebalancing.

clips.text_zh: 肥仔信成日問我幾時cut。我由83kg cut到65kg，再lean bulk返80kg。膊頭有肉但腹肌未出⋯⋯再食多2個月先？ok。
clips.text_en_b1: In May 2025 I was 83kg and fat, with almost no muscle. I cut aggressively until mid-April 2026, down to 65kg and skinnyfat. I could barely bench the 20kg bar. Now I lean bulked back up to 80kg. I bench 3x8 at one plate, squat 3x6 at 90kg, and deadlift 3x8 at 120kg.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ skinnyfat lifter unsure when to cut
clips.text_en_b2: In May 2025 I tipped the scales at a flabby 83kg with virtually no muscle to show for it, so I committed to an aggressive cut that dragged me down to 65kg by mid-April 2026, leaving me genuinely skinnyfat. I could barely bench the empty 20kg bar at that point. Since then I have leaned bulk back up to a solid 80kg, and my lifts have climbed accordingly: benching 3x8 at one plate, squatting 3x6 at 90kg, and pulling 3x8 at 120kg on deadlifts.
clips.text_en_c1: Back in May 2025 I tipped the scales at a decidedly unflattering 83kg—soft, untrained, and carrying negligible muscle mass. An aggressive cut followed, bringing me down to 65kg by mid-April 2026, at which point the mirror presented the classic skinnyfat paradox: lighter, certainly, but visually unremarkable. Since then I have reverse-dialled into a lean bulk, settling at 80kg, with my bench press having progressed to 3x8 at a single plate, squat to 3x6 at 90kg, and deadlift to 3x8 at 120kg. Shoulders and traps now read clearly, yet the abdominal definition remains stubbornly absent.
clips.text_en_c2: In May 2025 I tipped the scales at a corpulent eighty-three kilograms, adipose tissue predominating over any discernible muscular architecture. I thereafter commenced an aggressive hypocaloric regimen, sustaining the deficit with monastic discipline until mid-April 2026, at which juncture I had been whittled to a distinctly underwhelming sixty-five kilograms, the proverbial skinnyfat spectre made flesh, scarcely capable of pressing the unladen twenty-kilogram barbell. Subsequently I embarked upon a protracted lean bulk, methodically accruing mass to a present eighty kilograms, with current lifts resting at bench press three-by-eight at one plate, squat three-by-six at ninety kilograms, and deadlift three-by-eight at one hundred and twenty. My reflection has altered appreciably: deltoids now protrude with restrained vigour, yet the abdominal definition remains frustratingly elusive.

clips.text_zh: Soremachi出新video，Ishiguro自己排最愛角色再畫泳裝版。Kon-senpai又冇份⋯⋯Ebi-chan原來係佢小學初戀。睇完好治癒。
clips.text_en_b1: Ishiguro ranked his favourite characters from his own manga, Soremachi, and drew them in swimsuits. Kon-senpai is not in the main lineup, but her SD version from the gag manga appears. The creator said Ebi-chan is based on his first crush from elementary school. Anons are posting their own rankings in the thread.
clips.source_hint: /a/ Soremachi creator ranks his own characters
clips.text_en_b2: Ishiguro has dropped a brand-new video in which he ranks his own favourite characters from Soremachi, and as a sweet bonus he has sketched each one in swimsuits. Kon-senpai fans are up in arms because she is absent from the main lineup, although her SD counterpart from the gag manga does make a brief cameo. In a charming reveal, Ishiguro admitted that Ebi-chan was actually inspired by his very first crush back in elementary school, which sent the thread into a wholesome frenzy.
clips.text_en_c1: In a characteristically self-referential promotional move, Ishiguro—the creator of Soremachi—released a video in which he ranks his own creations from the manga, subsequently illustrating each in swimwear. Kon-senpai, notably absent from the principal lineup, nevertheless appears in her super-deformed iteration from the side gag parody. In a disclosure that the thread has predictably mined for biographical speculation, the artist confirmed that Ebi-chan is loosely modelled on his first childhood crush from elementary school. Anons, evidently energised, have responded with their own tier lists and spirited defences of overlooked favourites. The cumulative effect is less an announcement than a communal exercise in shared affection.
clips.text_en_c2: Ishiguro, the reclusive auteur behind Soremachi, has lately unveiled a bespoke ranking of his own creations, accompanied by freshly illustrated swimsuit renditions that have sent the fandom into paroxysms of febrile exegesis. Kon-senpai, perennial bridesmaid of the character polls, finds herself once again omitted from the principal lineup, though her super-deformed avatar from the comedic spinoff makes a token cameo. In a disclosure of unexpected intimacy, the creator confessed that Ebi-chan, that winsome everygirl, constitutes no fictional contrivance but rather a portrait of his inaugural elementary-school infatuation, a revelation that has occasioned considerable affectionate mirth among long-standing devotees.

clips.text_zh: Cramer話oil去$150。我做斜坡survey，成日揸車入地盤，油價一爆所有cost都升。個prop firm又輸⋯⋯double打擊。wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: Jim Cramer posted on X that oil at $150 is about to become reality. /biz/ is reacting hard because crude above $150 would break every diesel-dependent business. Slope surveys and site visits get more expensive overnight. Contractors will pass fuel costs into every GI report and every soil nailing quote.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ Cramer tweet on oil going to $150

signal.rationale: Civil-engineering framing of macro oil news, no trade

clips.text_en_b2: Jim Cramer took to X to declare that crude oil hitting $150 is no longer a hypothetical but an imminent reality, and /biz/ is losing its mind over the fallout. Because slope surveys and site visits require constant driving out to job sites, any diesel-dependent contractor would see costs balloon overnight. Fuel surcharges would inevitably get passed straight into every GI report, every soil nailing quote, and every line item on future bids.
clips.text_en_c1: Jim Cramer's X post positing oil at $150 has jolted /biz/ into its customary mode of reflexive apocalyptic modelling. Crude sustained above that threshold, the consensus holds, would render every diesel-intensive operation structurally unviable—slope survey logistics, site mobilisation and remote-site commuting would all absorb cost increases more or less overnight. Independent contractors, operating on already compressed margins, would have little choice but to embed fuel surcharges into every ground investigation report and soil nailing quotation they submit. For those simultaneously running leveraged positions through prop firms, the scenario amounts to a particularly unwelcome double-bind: rising operational costs compounded by deteriorating portfolio performance.
clips.text_en_c2: Jim Cramer, that venerable harbinger of either prescience or perdition depending upon one's priors, has taken to X to proclaim with characteristic bombast that crude at $150 per barrel is no longer hypothetical but imminent. The reaction across /biz/ has been apoplectic, given that sustained prices north of this threshold would eviscerate every diesel-dependent enterprise along the value chain. My own travails conducting slope stability surveys are instructive: site visits, already logistically punishing, become prohibitively expensive as fuel surcharges cascade through contractor invoicing. Each geotechnical instrumentation report, each soil nailing quotation, each line item in a geologist's interim submission shall henceforth bear the indelible imprint of refinery gate prices.
